arxiv.title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
arxiv.abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables ρn=sin²θn, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted ℓ¹ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the γ-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separate

arxiv.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
arxiv.abstract: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

arxiv.title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La₂SmNi₂O₇₋δ
arxiv.abstract: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature (Tcoⁿset) up to 96 K has been observed in the La₂₋ₓSm₁₊ₓNi₂O₇₋δ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the La₂SmNi₂O₇₋δ single crystal with Tcoⁿset=92.5 K under pressure. Within the Ullah–Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near TcMF. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the dz₂ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the dₓ₂₋y₂ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

arxiv.title: Probing Phase Fluctuations in Cuprates by Multidimensional Josephson Spectroscopy
arxiv.abstract: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. arxiv.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
arxiv.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from -155;dBm to -130;dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from -95;dBm to -55;dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of 6.0;GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of (74.7±0.2) ;dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of (75.4±6.8) ;dB. arxiv.title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
arxiv.abstract: Layered palladates provide a 4d platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO₂, RbSr₂PdO₃, BaLaPdO₂Cl₂, La₄Pd₃O₈, and La₅Pd₄O₁₀. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-dₓ₂₋y₂ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-dz₂ orbital. LaPdO₂ and BaLaPdO₂Cl₂ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr₂PdO₃ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La₄Pd₃O₈ and quadlayer La₅Pd₄O₁₀ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-dₓ₂₋y₂ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO₂Cl₂ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr₂PdO₃ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-dz₂ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

arxiv.title: Inversion of magnetization anisotropy in low magnetic fields for textured Bi2223 superconductor due to magnetic responses from superconducting crystallites and intercrystalline boundaries
arxiv.abstract: A detailed study of the magnetic anisotropy of a bulk textured high-temperature superconductor Bi2223 has been carried out. In the range of moderate and high fields (up to 1 kOe), the difference ΔM between the upper and lower branches of the magnetization hysteresis loop is larger when the external magnetic field H is parallel to the normal of the texturing plane (H||NTP) than when H is parallel to the texturing plane (H {\perp} NTP). This magnetic anisotropy is typical for such textured superconductors. However, at small values of the maximum applied field Hmax (up to 15 Oe at a temperature T = 78 K), an anomalous inversion of anisotropy has been found: ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H {\perp} NTP). It has been established that in the field range up to ~30 Oe (the first penetration field into Bi2223 crystallites is about 30 Oe at T = 78 K), the magnetic hysteresis is determined only by the magnetic flux trapped in the intercrystallite boundary subsystem. The pronounced platelet shape of the Bi2223 crystallites leads to partial screening of the external field inside the sample when the field is oriented parallel to the crystallite c-axis. The observed inverse anisotropy ΔM(H||NTP) < ΔM(H {\perp} NTP) has been explained by the fact that the effective magnetic field into the intercrystallite boundaries is smaller for the H||NTP orientation than for H {\perp} NTP. arxiv.title: Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures
arxiv.abstract: In Eliashberg theory of phonon-mediated superconductivity with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential, the critical temperature Tc marks the linear instability of the normal state. Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan (KAY) characterized it through the top eigenvalue of a compact operator on Matsubara-frequency sequences. They proved that Tc is unique at strong coupling and conjectured Tc<C(λ⟨ω²⟩)¹/² for every coupling λ, with ⟨ω²⟩ the second moment of the normalized phonon spectrum and C≈0.1827 sharp, a bound Leavens stated in 1977 on partly numerical grounds. A preprint by Kondratev, not yet peer reviewed, gives a proof of this bound and of all-coupling uniqueness. We give an independent proof, for every spectrum with finite second moment, based on a comparison principle that is also Kondratev's central step and was proved to first order by Bergmann and Rainer: strengthening the pairing interaction at every Matsubara transfer, strictly at the smallest one, strictly raises the top eigenvalue. At fixed λ and ⟨ω²⟩ a single Einstein mode maximizes Tc. arxiv.title: Phase diagram and lattice structure of interlayer vortices in multilayer Ising superconductors in parallel magnetic fields
arxiv.abstract: In this work, we investigate layered s-wave Ising superconductors under an in-plane magnetic field using self-consistent solutions of the microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations. Comparing bilayer, four-layer, and infinite-layer systems, we determine how the phase diagram and vortex structure evolve with layer number. Compared to standard Ginzburg-Landau treatments, our approach applies over a broader parameter regime and self-consistently resolves the spatial and layer dependence of the gap amplitude without prescribing its form. We find that the field range supporting the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) phase (defined as having no interlayer vortices) is reduced with increasing layer number and is essentially absent at nonzero magnetic flux in the infinite-layer system, consistent with recent thickness-dependent experiments on multilayer 2H-NbSe₂. In the infinite-layer limit, the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase containing interlayer vortices persists to progressively larger in-plane fields as temperature is lowered below the zero-field critical temperature, consistent with the experimentally observed low-temperature enhancement of the upper critical field. arxiv.title: Exceptional structure and Lifshitz criticality in a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain
arxiv.abstract: We study an exactly solvable non-Hermitian N-site Kitaev chain with unequal pair-creation and pair-annihilation amplitudes and vanishing intersite hopping. We show that the chain supports an exceptional point (EP) at which all the many-body energies collapse to zero and the largest Jordan block grows quadratically with N. By constructing an explicit positive metric for the associated N-dimensional one-body problem which admits an extension to the full many-body Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that this EP collapse can be approached through a continuous quasi-Hermitian path in the parameter space. Further, in a different regime with onsite energies alternating between two unequal positive values, we show that pairing amplitudes of opposite signs can lead to crossings between ground states of opposite fermion parity within a quasi-Hermitian regime. Their accumulation in the thermodynamic limit produces a Lifshitz transition, characterized by particle-/hole-pocket formation, quadratic critical dispersion, and a nonanalytic ground-state energy density. We show that this transition remains separated from the EP boundary and ceases to exist for balanced real pairing.

arxiv.title: Stabilization of LaH₁₀ with Thorium: Superconductivity in (La,Th)H₁₀ up to 232 K near 1 Mbar
arxiv.abstract: Ternary lanthanum-based hydrides are among the best high-temperature superconductors. Here we show that substituting La with thorium stabilizes La(Th)H₁₀ clathrate structure at ∼1 Mbar while only minimally suppressing superconductivity. The resulting cubic (La,Th)H₁₀ phase, synthesized from relatively air-stable La₂Th, La₃Th and La₅Th alloys, reaches an onset textitT_c = 232 K at 134 GPa, as confirmed by contact resistance measurements. Superconductivity was verified by two independent methods: electrical resistance and contactless radio-frequency measurements under applied magnetic fields at various pressures. Using a record-high pulsed current of 380 mA, we investigated critical phenomena in P6₃/mmc-(La,Th)H₉ at 173 GPa, which allowed for the experimental determination of a single superconducting gap within the s-wave model: Δ(0) = 37 ±4.5 meV and 2Δ(0)/kTc = 4.9 ±0.6. The La-Th-H system is chemically rich: in addition to the decahydride and nonahydride mentioned above, we also identified nanocrystalline I4/mmm-(La,Th)H₄ (5-6 nm grain size), (La,Th)H₆, as well as hP13, cF80 and A15 phases with compositions of (La,Th)H₅.₇₅₋₆.₂₅ and textitT_c ≈ 83 K at 70-80 GPa, and a possible (La,Th)H₁₆ polyhydride.

arxiv.title: High Characteristic Voltage YBCO Josephson Junctions Written With a Focused Helium Ion Beam
arxiv.abstract: We report in-plane Josephson junctions written directly into YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋δ (YBCO) thin films with a focused helium ion beam (He FIB). The characteristic voltage ICR of these junctions, where IC is the Josephson critical current and R is the junction resistance, sets the operating frequency and the sensitivity of the circuits built from them. A single line irradiation with a dose of \SI{500}{ions/nm} across a \SI{4}{\micro\metre} wide electrode produced a junction with ICR of 929 \si{\micro\volt} at \SI{1.6}{K}, which is `higher than the 200 to 400 \si{\micro\volt} typical of junctions fabricated previously in our laboratory. Temperature dependent resistance, current-voltage characteristics, magnetic field modulation of the critical current, and Shapiro steps under 20.5~GHz microwave irradiation show Josephson behavior with an excess current below 5 percent of the critical current. The critical current falls steeply with temperature near the junction transition and saturates at low temperature. We attribute this behavior to a barrier at the metal insulator transition, where hopping conduction through localized states is active at finite temperature and freezes out on cooling. We describe the changes in surface preparation, sample selection, beam focusing, and sample storage that accompanied the improvement, although the present data do not separate their individual contributions.

arxiv.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
arxiv.abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent ν>0, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. arxiv.title: Optical response of quantum metals
arxiv.abstract: Strongly interacting quantum systems display puzzling electrical transport properties whose interpretation remains controversial. Many theoretical and phenomenological analyses assume that the complex behaviour observed in such `quantum materials' originates either from quasi-particles dressed with an anomalous electron self-energy or from collective excitations associated with hydrodynamic flow. Despite their distinctly different starting points, the underlying assumption is that dissipation of electrical current arises from the relaxation of the total momentum of charge carriers. This classical description breaks down in the absence of long-lived charge carriers. In such strange metals dissipation seems to be governed by the rate at which equilibrium is thermally restored, and it has been suggested that this constitutes an upper bound, known as the `Planckian limit'. Here we show that in this quantum regime a description of the conductivity in terms of relaxation rates no longer suffices: strange metal transport is carried instead by fast-decaying current fluctuations, which together with quantum detailed balance give rise to the widely observed Planckian dissipation. The distinction between classical and quantum metals becomes transparent when experimental data is analysed in terms of the current-current correlation function instead of the optical conductivity. arxiv.title: Quantum Fluctuations drive Emerging Bosonic Quantum Phases in a Moiré Flatband Superconductor
arxiv.abstract: Quantum fluctuations play a central role in superconductors by mediating the interactions that promote electron pairing and controlling the phase coherence required for macroscopic condensation. Thus far, understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations and superconductivity remains challenging in unconventional superconductors. Here, we establish quantum phase fluctuations as the organizing principle linking superconductivity and Bose-insulating quantum criticality in a moiré flatband superconductor of alternating twisted trilayer graphene (ATTG). Superconductivity is optimal near half-filling of the moiré flatband and gives way to a density-wave-like resistance peak at high temperatures, in which we observe distinct temperature scales for the pairing (~6 K) and the condensation (~1 K). We observe compelling evidence of a bosonic superconducting quantum phase transition, driven by both out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields, with a universal critical resistivity of Rc = 0.62RQ and finite-temperature scaling of zνB = 2.3, where RQ = h/4e² is the quantum resistance for bosons. Strikingly, the observed bosonic insulator shows a nearly quantized resistivity of RQ that saturates at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, together with a zero-bias peak, a nearly zero Hall resistance, and a logarithmic dependence at higher temperatures. arxiv.title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
arxiv.abstract: We formulate a charge-4e parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS [[11,1,5]]₃ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator. Its all-syndrome acceptance is distinct from the known 1/1728 ideal acceptance of one-round strange-state Golay distillation. An accepted-run target-infidelity budget and a synthetic parameter protocol expose the remaining noise assumptions. Native charge-4e syndrome extraction, material feasibility, a device threshold, and unconditional fault tolerance are not established.

arxiv.title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
arxiv.abstract: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in La₃Ni₂O₇ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting Ba at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in mathrmLa₃₋ₓBaₓNi₂O₇ at a small doping ratio of x ∼0.15. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue λ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature Tc to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that s±-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required Ba concentration (x ∼0.15) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

arxiv.title: Non-ergodic Area Scaling of Andreev Transport in Al/AlOₓ/Al Tunnel Junctions
arxiv.abstract: State-of-the-art superconducting qubits rely on Al/AlOₓ/Al Josephson junctions (JJs) as a nonlinear element with an ideal sinusoidal current-phase dependence, with its inductance set by the junction area and oxidation conditions. This idealization holds only if the many conduction channels through the amorphous AlOₓ barrier transmit weakly and almost identically. Here, we measure the second-order subgap Andreev current, which sets the second Josephson harmonic, in Al/AlOₓ/Al JJs. For junction sizes relevant to qubits, we find that this current is dominated by ≲300 effective channels whose transparencies exceed the ideal tunneling limit (≲10⁻⁶) by orders of magnitude. For small and high-aspect-ratio junctions, increasing the junction size does not average out the effect of these high transparency channels but instead adds additional channels of even greater transparency. The trend inverts once both the width and length of the junction exceed a critical length scale, above which the effective transparency decreases with area. This non-ergodic scaling of the Andreev current is reproduced by simulations and attributed to non-self-averaging statistics of the transparency distribution, which arise from variations in oxide thickness. The effect is largely invisible to the normal-state conductance used to target the inductance and reveals unexpected geometric and size-related trade-off

arxiv.title: Reflection Zeros Set the Scattering Invariant of Finite Majorana Wires
arxiv.abstract: Majorana modes, zero-energy excitations of superconducting wires that are their own antiparticles, could store quantum information protected from local noise. In transport experiments, however, ordinary bound states mimic their signature, a conductance peak at zero voltage, and whether Majorana modes have been observed remains debated. A sign, Q, of the electron reflection at zero energy marks the topological phase of a long wire, but what Q certifies in a finite device has been unclear. Here we show for the first time that Q counts reflectionless states, waves that enter through one contact and leave entirely through the other: Q=-1 when an odd number of them lie in the lower half of the complex energy plane. In a finite wire this means that the two Majorana modes are split by less than their coupling to the contacts. With equal contacts, every sign change of Q, including the bulk topological transition, is an exceptional point at which two such states merge and transmission is maximally flat. At zero temperature, Q=-1 exactly when the zero-bias conductance measured at a contact exceeds e²/h. These results show what transport can certify about a Majorana device and how to read the invariant from conductance.

Large language models (LLMs) can read those papers, and databases built that way are appearing. The difficulty is not the reading but the trust: a number lifted out of a sentence can belong to a neighbouring compound, a computed transition temperature can be recorded without saying that it is computed, and the paper itself may be wrong. This paper describes a pipeline that extracts superconducting materials from the published literature with an LLM, checks every value against its source, and asks how far that checking goes. The pipeline proposed 19,576 records; a cascade of gates rejected 659,252 field-level extractions, 644,438 of them for want of verbatim evidence, 13,121 because the text does not attach the value to the material, and 1,693 because the source sentence reads as a calculation. ai.abstract: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets (R² = 0.96 with NIMS SuperCon). Using AutoSuperCon, we show that median gap ratios rise from 3.6 in conventional superconductors to 6.4 in cuprates, 28% of upper critical fields exceed the Pauli limit, and critical temperatures lie below a ceiling proportional to the superfluid density. Further, we train composition-based predictors for the critical temperature (R²log=0.83) and the upper critical field (R²log=0.69), boosted by transfer learning. Within known superconducting families, composition alone is sufficient to screen candidates for both parameters. AutoSuperCon thus enables physical insight and data-driven discovery across thousands of superconductors.

ai.title: Predictions of superconducting properties from chemical bonding interactions
ai.abstract: The need for rapid estimates of superconducting critical temperatures, Tc s, is becoming increasingly urgent as first-principles and artificial intelligence based methods enable the exploration of ever-larger and more chemically complex materials spaces. In this context, chemical bonding based quantities have emerged as promising descriptors for predicting superconductivity. To date, these approaches have mainly been developed for hydride superconductors, notably through the networking value, a descriptor based upon the electron localization function, whose topological properties have been found to correlate with Tc . In this perspective, we review and consolidate the method's theory, and we discuss how the estimate of the Tc is achievable within a real-space view. We conclude by proposing a framework that enables Tc prediction for the broad family of conventional superconductors from easily computable intermediate physical quantities.

ai.abstract: Neural networks trained to predict materials properties learn representations whose physical content can be difficult to extract. We use the neural tangent kernel (NTK), evaluated at trained parameters, to recover the geometry learned by a network that predicts superconducting transition temperatures from elemental composition alone. Kernel ridge regression with the trained NTK closely reproduces the network's predictive performance and substantially outperforms regression with the initial kernel. Clustering and local neighborhood analysis organize compounds into recognizable superconducting families and connect materials with related chemical and correlated-electron properties despite substantial differences in Tc. These results establish trained tangent kernels as practical probes of learned materials representations, connecting property prediction with the exploration of materials space.

ai.abstract: Muon-spin rotation/relaxation is one of the most powerful microscopic probes for understanding magnetic order, spin dynamics, superconductivity, and complex magnetic phases in emerging quantum materials. ai.abstract: Generative models now propose millions of "stable" crystal structures, and their own referees have shown that stability is not discovery; no public benchmark asks whether a candidate has the physics to do a job. ai.title: Machine learning reveals common features of unconventional superconductors with high transition temperatures
ai.abstract: Superconductors with high critical temperatures that emerges beyond the phonon-mediated regime are usually considered unconventional in nature, yet unlike conventional superconductors, no broadly applicable predictive theory currently guides their discovery. Here, we use interpretable machine learning to uncover a common materials-space signature of high-Tc unconventional superconductors and develop a data-driven strategy for materials discovery. We construct a unified feature representation for each material by integrating compositional statistics, structural information, and latent representations from trained property-prediction models, followed by structure-aware filtering of an experimentally established superconducting dataset. Without using transition-temperature information, unsupervised analysis shows that cuprate and iron-based superconductors occupy a common region of materials space, characterized primarily by large electronegativity deviation and intermediate mean valence-electron number. A supervised Tc model independently identifies the same descriptors as dominant features, providing complementary evidence for their relevance. Using this empirical materials-space prior together with the Tc model, we prioritize candidate materials, recover recently discovered nickelate superconductors, and identify chemically distinct candidates for future investigation.

ai.title: First-Principles Electron-Magnon Coupling with Machine-Learning Hamiltonians: From Band Renormalization to Transport
ai.abstract: In analogy to electron-phonon coupling (EPC), electron-magnon coupling (EMC) is expected to shape electronic structure, transport, and possibly unconventional superconductivity in magnetic materials. However, unlike EPC, which is now routinely treated within first-principles frameworks, a quantitative description of EMC, especially for transport, remains elusive because of the lack of theoretical formalism. Consequently, even for elemental iron, EPC-only calculations miss both the magnitude and the T² component of resistivity. This discrepancy has long been attributed to EMC, although direct computational evidence has been lacking and the underlying transport mechanism remains unresolved. Here we develop a unified first-principles formalism for EMC in collinear magnetic systems within many-body perturbation theory, complemented by machine-learning spinful Hamiltonians that supply quantities not directly accessible from conventional first-principles methods. Our framework enables ab initio transport calculations including EMC effects for the first time. Applied to ferromagnetic α-Fe, our approach yields electron spectral functions consistent with previous studies. ai.title: Properties of holographic superconductors from Machine Learning
ai.abstract: We investigate holographic superconductors using modern optimisation techniques inspired by machine learning. The critical temperature is obtained by minimising the variational functional for the eigenvalue λ² with two complementary trial functions: a simple cosine ansatz F(z)=cos(a z) and a flexible exponential polynomial F(z)=exp(sumn₌₂N an zⁿ), both of which automatically satisfy the standard boundary conditions. For the cosine ansatz, we perform a one-parameter minimisation and obtain λ²(Δ) and Tc/√ρ over a wide range of Δ, including the exact values at Δ=1 and Δ=2 to high accuracy. The exponential polynomial ansatz, with up to 19 coefficients, is optimised using a multi-start L-BFGS-B algorithm with warm-starting, yielding even better agreement with known exact results. Our numerical data for λ²(Δ) and Tc/√ρ match the analytical predictions from the literature, confirming the robustness of the variational approach. This work; therefore, demonstrates that a combination of analytic trial functions and modern numerical optimisation provides a powerful, flexible, and efficient tool for exploring holographic superconductors, and can be readily extended to include backreaction or other sectors in this field.

ai.title: Superconductivity in the t-t' Hubbard Model from Symmetry-Preserving Neural-Network Quantum States
ai.abstract: Despite its fundamental importance in the theory of strongly correlated electrons, the nature of the ground state of the two-dimensional doped Hubbard model remains intensely debated. Variational approaches provide a powerful route to this problem, but their conclusions can depend sensitively on the chosen wave-function parameterization, the mean-field initialization, or the pinning fields used to guide the optimization, as well as on boundary conditions. This can favor one type of symmetry breaking over another, making it difficult to distinguish the genuine interplay of intertwined or competing orders from biases induced by the variational parameterization. Here, we introduce the Symmetry-Preserving Backflow Pairing (SBP) ansatz, a neural-network wave function that respects translational symmetry by construction and thereby avoids these broken-symmetry minima. The SBP ansatz reaches state-of-the-art variational energies for the t-t' Hubbard model on lattices up to 24×24 with 504 electrons, below those of competing pure stripe solutions. By extrapolating to the thermodynamic limit, we find robust evidence for d-wave superconducting order, resolving a long-standing question about the 1/8-doped model at t'/t=-0.2 and U/t=8.0. ai.title: Quadrupolar phase transition in superconducting lanthanum hydride
ai.abstract: Lanthanum hydride (LaH₁₀) has been widely studied for its high superconducting critical temperature of 250 K at about 170 GPa pressure. Although the structural Rbar3m-to-Fmbar3m transition under pressure connected to the emergence of the superconducting phase in this material is broadly understood, the detailed characterization of its nature and its order parameter are still missing. By applying the cluster multipole moment analysis to the hydrogen sublattice, we reveal that this transition is triggered by a quadrupolar T₂g order parameter, and we provide evidence for its weak first-order nature. By performing path integral molecular dynamics coupled to a message-passing atomic cluster expansion (MACE) neural network potential, trained on Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) density functional theory configurations, we show that the collapse of the order parameter at the transition is simultaneously associated with the discontinuous softening of the optical T₂g phonons. Their symmetry lets them carry a non-negligible electron-phonon coupling in LaH₁₀, while the weak first-order nature of the transition makes them soft. The presence of structural instabilities with low-frequency quadrupolar distortions can be a key ingredient to enhance superconductivity in superhydrides and provides guidance for the discovery of new high-Tc superconductors in hydrogen-rich compounds.

ai.title: Avoiding Dilution: Using Diffusion and Vision Transformers to resolve Majorana Features in Nanowires at High Temperature
ai.abstract: Identifying Majorana zero modes in semiconductor–superconductor nanowires requires ultra-low temperature transport measurements in dilution refrigerators, making device screening slow and resource-intensive. Here, we investigate whether high-temperature conductance data can be used to infer low-temperature Majorana nanowire properties before committing devices to dilution-refrigerator characterization. We generate paired high- and low-temperature conductance simulations for disordered Majorana nanowires and train neural networks to perform two related tasks. First, we use a Shifted Window U-Net Transformer diffusion-inspired architecture to reconstruct low-temperature conductance from thermally broadened high-temperature measurements, achieving high-fidelity recovery with R² ≈0.95 for local conductance and R² ≈0.91 for nonlocal conductance. Second, we train a Video Vision Transformer-based network to predict the low-temperature topological visibility directly from high-temperature conductance, obtaining R² ≈0.80. These results demonstrate that machine-learning models can recover and infer low-temperature Majorana features from experimentally easier high-temperature data, providing a practical route for rejecting poor devices early thus avoiding slow and resource-intensive dilution refrigeration for non-promising devices.
